name: Board Track Path
description: The board as a graph, not a grid. Spaces are nodes, movement edges may branch or run one-way, and each space carries an effect id that is broadcast when a token lands — this component owns the topology and the landing resolution, and borrows world.tile_grid only for coordinates and rendering, because loops, branches, and one-way edges are things a raw grid cannot express. Branch choices are data-driven (player choice, die result, or fixed) and raised as an event so the turn UI can ask the active player. It does not own token positions — movement.token_movement does, and announces arrivals via movement.tokenMoved — and it does not know what 'draw a card' or 'pay 200' mean: it emits the space's effect id and lets inventory.card_draw_deck or economy.currency do their own jobs.

inputs.name: trackGraph
inputs.description: Nodes with ids, grid coordinates, effect ids, and outgoing edges; edges may be marked one-way or branch. Required because a track with no topology is a floor tile with ambitions.

inputs.name: startSpaceId
inputs.description: The space tokens begin on and lap past. Named explicitly because 'the first node in the list' is an accident, not a design.

inputs.name: branchChoiceMode
inputs.description: player | die | fixed — who or what picks at a branch. player asks via world.branchChoiceRequested; die defers to utility.dice_roll_resolver; fixed follows the edge order in trackGraph.

outputs.name: branchSpaceIds
outputs.description: Spaces with more than one outgoing edge — the decision points, surfaced so UI can telegraph them before arrival.
